about: Cover's own models, round 1. Numbers from ml/RESULTS.md (and the files it was written from) and from ml/ocr/worker.py's end-to-end run. Rates are percentages with Wilson 95% intervals; Gini intervals are 200-resample bootstrap 95% intervals.
synthetic: All training and test data is synthetic: code-generated people, policies, claims and documents, with no real personal data and no real claims experience. Round 1 was generated in the shape of the first (Taiwan) market. Cover is now a US product; the US-shaped round (ZIP-level flood, wildfire, hurricane, earthquake and theft; square feet and miles; English US receipts, invoices and police reports in USD with MM/DD/YYYY dates) is being generated and trained, and its numbers will replace these.

teacher.name: Muse Glimmer
teacher.role: the only teacher: it writes people's words around facts code made, and answers the audit cases. No Claude or GPT output is used as training data.

models.name: Cover-OCR
models.does: Reads a photo of a claim document (receipt, invoice, repair quote, police report) into the reader's fields: date, amount, currency, merchant, tax id, report number, items, text.
models.base: None: an SVTR-tiny-style line recogniser (conv stem, local and global mixing, CTC), trained from scratch in PyTorch. 4.0M parameters, 396 characters. No line detector yet: the app's worker finds lines by projection.
models.data: 5,000 synthetic documents (50,129 lines) in six fonts, photographed with perspective, creases, glare, blur, noise and JPEG; test 400 new documents; test_font 200 in a font never trained on. Round 1 is Traditional Chinese (Taiwan) documents.
models.verdict: Not the app's reader. End to end (photo, lines found by projection, CPU) it gets every field of a document right on 44.5% [39.7, 49.4] of held-out documents, and 0% on an unseen font; with the true line positions it is 75.3%. It also reads Chinese documents, and Cover's documents are now English US ones. Muse Glimmer stays the reader until an English Cover-OCR is trained and measured the same way.

models.name: Cover-1B
models.does: A small language model for four jobs: answering questions on the policy's clauses, turning a claim story into fields, turning OCR text into the reader's JSON, and the quote dialogue; resisting instructions planted in documents and stories.
models.base: Llama 3.2 1B Instruct and Qwen3-1.7B, LoRA r16 (both trained, the better one kept)
models.data: Facts made by code (Cover's products, clauses and claim engine), put into people's words by Muse Glimmer, filtered by code; held-out sets and held-out injection templates.
models.verdict: Training on the VM; no scores yet.

models.name: Cover-Risk
models.does: Each policy's expected yearly claims, for pricing, with its reasons (path attributions as multiplying factors). Not a language model.
models.base: None: LightGBM, Tweedie loss (power 1.5), monotone in hazard levels, past claims, age and sums insured; a Poisson x Gamma GLM as the baseline. Evaluated in plain Node from exported trees.
models.data: Per product, 200,000 synthetic training and 50,000 test policies from a stated generator (Poisson frequency, Gamma severity, the product's factor table times hidden effects). Life is not modelled: it is priced from a mortality table.

scores.home_level_note: Home is scaled by 1.0795 (actual / predicted on its 200,000 training policies) before it prices a quote, as RESULTS.md asks.

models.verdict: LightGBM and the GLM are within noise of each other and of the true premium's ceiling, except car, where LightGBM is ahead ([+0.003, +0.010] Gini) with 30% lower error. These numbers show only that the model learnt the generator's assumptions.

models.name: Cover-Audit
models.does: Checks a claim decision the engine made: agrees, or names the wrong clause, an over- or under-payment, or a claim that should go to a person.
models.base: Llama 3.2 1B, LoRA, losses only at the verdict and the check markers
models.data: Cases run through Cover's own claim engine with made-up people, most decisions spoiled one way; test 300 x 3 Glimmer answers, val 200 x 2, train 2,000. Glimmer's agreement with itself is the ceiling.
models.verdict: Training on the VM; no scores yet.
